## 6. Summary and self-check
Format checklist, one-paragraph essence, self-check tasks.
examShortTricks: Trick 1: Structure: each stanza pairs a GIFT the speaker offers with the war's grim 'gift' returned — the ironic exchange is the poem's device; explain one pair.
Trick 2: Anti-war message through personal loss: flowers and youth exchanged for a grave and death — the contrast between tender gifts and war's returns is the theme.
Trick 3: The address to the dead beloved (apostrophe) makes grief intimate — name the device and its emotional effect.
practiceQuestions: Q. What 'gifts' does war return to the speaker? (2 marks) — her beloved's grave, the smell of death, a lost youth — war's cruel exchanges.
Q. What is the tone of the poem? (1 mark) — mournful and bitterly ironic.
keyPoints: Dialogue with a dead soldier-husband — irony in 'gifts': medals for a life.
Anti-war theme: war's gifts are worthless against human loss; point out the reversal.
